captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 5.
In this lesson: Inventions that changed our lives.
Use the present perfect to talk about experiences and changes up to now.
Here are some new words. Invent. Make something new that did not exist before. Inventor.
A person who invents things. Machine. A thing with parts that move to do a job.
Listen and say them. invent
inventor
machine.
And some more words. Design. Plan how something will look and work. Improve.
Make something better. Electricity. Energy that makes lights and machines work.
Listen and say them. design
improve
electricity.
Time for a question. The video will stop.
Which word means: make something new that did not exist before?
Now some grammar: Present perfect.
Use have or has, plus the past participle, for experiences and changes up to now.
Use ‘ever’ in questions and ‘never’ in negatives.
For example: Have you ever used a 3D printer? For example: Phones have changed a lot.
For example: I have never seen a robot dog.
Now listen, and read along. Small inventions, big changes.
Some inventions are so normal that we hardly notice them.
But they have changed our lives in big ways.
The light bulb: Before electric light, people used candles and oil lamps.
Electric light has made it possible to read, work and play safely after dark.
The bicycle: The first bicycles had no pedals. People pushed them along with their feet!
Since then, inventors have improved the design many times.
The zip: Before the zip, clothes and bags had lots of buttons and hooks.
The zip has made getting dressed much faster.
Which invention have you used today?
Another question. The video will stop. What did people use before electric light?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like invent, inventor, machine.
You practised the present perfect. And you read Small inventions, big changes.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!

captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 5. In this lesson: How does it work?
Read an explanation text and recognise the passive: is made, are used.
Here are some new words. Explain. Make something clear so people understand. Process.
A series of steps to make something happen. Material. What something is made of.
Listen and say them. explain
process
material.
And some more words. Recycle. Use something again to make something new. Factory.
A building where things are made by machines. Melt. Change from solid to liquid when hot.
Listen and say them. recycle
factory
melt.
Time for a question. The video will stop.
Which word means: make something clear so people understand?
Now some grammar: The passive, in the present.
Use is or are, plus the past participle, when the action is more important than who does it.
For example: Paper is made from wood. For example: Bottles are collected every week.
Now listen, and read along. How a plastic bottle is recycled.
Every day, millions of plastic bottles are used around the world.
Here is how many of them are recycled.
First, the bottles are collected from recycling bins and taken to a special factory.
Next, they are sorted by colour and washed to remove labels and dirt.
Then the bottles are cut into tiny flakes.
The flakes are melted and made into small pellets. Finally,
the pellets are sold to companies, where they are used to make new things – like bottles,
T-shirts and even park benches!
Another question. The video will stop. Where are the bottles taken?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like explain, process, material.
You practised the passive. And you read How a plastic bottle is recycled.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!
